text:
Maya (support): Heads-up — Acme reported sustained 429s after a marketing send. They say it started ~09:12 PST. They're on the Free tier and hit a sharp burst so their app is failing. Paste of customer error below.

acme-support (customer): 'We got continuous 429s and a bunch of user errors; our dashboard shows requests spiking to ~2k req/min. We're blocked. Sample response: {\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\", \"retry_after\":12} Headers: x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d x-rate-limit-limit: 100 x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 x-rate-limit-reset: 1670000000'

Ravi (support): Thanks. Can you drop a raw curl (headers + payload) and the request id? Also need the account id and which API key they used so we can find the tenant.

acme-support (customer): 'curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"...","max_tokens":256}' -v' request-id=req_0a1b2c3d

Maya (support): Repro steps look good. From logs, they're on free-plan default quotas: 100 requests/min, 10 concurrent. Their traffic pattern has a large short burst (lots of small requests). Our prefix batching doesn't help because they're using many independent short calls.

Maya (support): We should propose a temporary quota bump while Sales engages for a paid upgrade. Sam, can Sales take this on? Customer says they want to move to paid but need a quick stop-gap so their app doesn't fail during the day-of-campaign.

Sam (sales): I can own this. Quick notes: Acme has engaged for an annual plan but contract not signed yet. We can authorize a time-limited staging uplift (up to 72h) without a signed MSA if billing approves. Please capture exact limits requested.

Ravi (support): Customer requests to sustain ~2000 req/min for next 24–48h and increase concurrent to 100. Proposed internal action: create a Billing Exception and apply a temporary quota grant tied to their API key and account id.

Elliot (billing): We can approve a 48h temporary grace increase pending Sales. For anything beyond that or sustained capacity we require at minimum a PO or signed contract. I'll need the account id, admin email, and a short justification. I'll create an exception ticket BE-9876.

Maya (support): Doing the uplift now. Using supportctl to attach ephemeral grant:

```
# internal action (example)
supportctl grants create \
  --account acme-12345 \
  --api-key sk-acme-XXXX \
  --limit-requests-per-minute 2000 \
  --concurrency 100 \
  --expires 2026-03-18T09:00:00Z \
  --reason "marketing spike - temporary uplift approved by Billing BE-9876"
```

Ravi (support): Applied. I also added a short-lived tag on the key so we can auto-revoke if we detect sustained high usage beyond the window. :lock:

Maya (support): Heads-up to eng-oncall — we added a temporary quota and will monitor latency and error rate. If you see tail latency degrade or CPU on the serving pool spike, please throttle or route to cheaper model variant.

eng-oncall (support-bot): Alert rule confirmed. I'll watch token/CPU. Auto-fallback policy is enabled: route to redwood-small-quant if latency > 300ms for 5m.

Sam (sales): I'll reach out to Acme and fast-track the commercial terms. Sam -> @legal to prioritize MSA review. Also recommend offering them a Dedicated trial if they need predictability.

Maya (support): Customer notified: temporary uplift applied, please test and confirm. Suggested repro steps we asked them to run: 1) use same curl with a controlled load (50 threads) 2) check response headers for x-rate-limit-* 3) share request-ids for any remaining 429s.

acme-support (customer): 'Thanks, uplift applied — immediate improvement. Still seeing a couple of 429s during peak second spike, sending request ids now.'

Ravi (support): Closing this thread from support side with follow-ups: BE-9876 (billing exception), SALES-1142 (commercial), and internal postmortem item to evaluate free-tier burst smoothing. Next steps: Sales to close contract, Billing to convert exception to billing terms or revoke after expiry, Support to monitor. :thumbsup:

Maya (support): Note for knowledge base: add a small doc snippet about temporary quota grants for free-tier customers to reduce support friction (who can approve, max window, audit trail).

Elliot (billing): Done — BE-9876 created and approval recorded. I'll keep the exception open for 48h unless Sales pushes for extension.

Ravi (support): Thanks team. Ticketing: internal case SUP-56421 links to BE-9876 and SALES-1142. Marking as 'escalated -> on hold (sales)'.
